none: This segment contains only the Arabic verse text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic usages illustrate shطر as toward a destination, including movement toward kings and the direction of a gaze.
rows.anchor: وأظعن بالقوم شطر الملوك أي نحوهم، وقال: إن العشير بها داء مخامرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatra ʿan means to move away, shatra ilayhi to approach; shāṭir and shatīr denote one far away or absent from home.
rows.anchor: ويقال: شطر عنه: بعد، وشطر إليه: أقبل، والشاطر من الشباب: البعيد من الجيران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥarām and al-ḥaram denote what is prohibited or inaccessible.
rows.anchor: الحرام والحرم والحرم: الممتنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-imtirāʾ derives from al-mirya, doubt; امترى means to doubt, and افتعل can carry the reciprocal sense of تفاعل.
rows.anchor: الامتراء: افتعال من المرية، وهي الشك. امترى في الشيء: شك فيه

rows.speaker: المازني، المبرد، الفارسي
rows.claim: They understand وجهة as the place toward which one turns, so its initial wāw is a root letter rather than a verbal-noun remnant.
rows.anchor: قال قوم، منهم المازني والمبرد والفارسي: إن وجهة اسم للمكان المتوجه إليه

rows.speaker: قوم، منهم المازني
rows.claim: Another grammatical analysis takes وجهة as a verbal noun; on this reading Sibawayh's reported examples make its retained wāw exceptional.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم، منهم المازني، فيما نقل المهدوي إلى أنه مصدر، وهو الذي يظهر من كلام سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the retained wāw in وجهة as regular for a verbal noun not derived from an attested verb وجه يجه; its actual verbs are توجه and اتجه, with sources التوجه and الاتجاه.
rows.anchor: أنه مصدر ليس بجار على فعله، إذ لا يحفظ وجه يجه، فيكون المصدر جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a direction the source وجهة extends a verbal noun to the place meant, like using a source for a passive noun.
rows.anchor: وإطلاقه على المكان المتوجه إليه هو من باب إطلاق المصدر على اسم المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استباق derives from سبق and may mean either reaching first, like سبق, or mutual competition, like تسابق.
rows.anchor: الاستباق: افتعال من السبق، وهو الوصول إلى الشيء أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الخيرات is the plural of خيرة and may follow فعلة or a reduced فيعلة pattern; خير and خيرة can mean good rather than comparative better.
rows.anchor: الخيرات: جمع خيرة، ويحتمل أن يكون بناء على فعلة، أو بناء على فيعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الجوع means drought; the need or desire to eat is properly called الغرث, though later writers use الجوع more broadly.
rows.anchor: القحط، وأما الحاجة إلى الأكل فإنما اسمها: الغرث

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: The Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months after arriving in Medina, wished to face the Kaaba, and then received the revelation directing him toward it; Jews asked what had turned them from their former qibla.
rows.anchor: رواه البخاري، عن البراء بن عازب قال: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة، فصلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers Jews and Christians who claimed Abraham and the earlier believers belonged to their religions; because Jews denied abrogation, they called the qibla change false and foolish, and God distinguishes guidance from folly.
rows.anchor: لأن النسخ عند اليهود باطل، فقالوا: الانتقال عن قبلتنا باطل وسفه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: On the apparent future reading, God foretold the Jews' objection before the order to face the Kaaba, making it a prediction of the unseen and preparing the Prophet and Muslims for the objection with an answer ready.
rows.anchor: وذلك قبل أن يؤمروا باستقبال الكعبة، وتكون هذه الآية متقدمة في النزول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: An alternative chronology places the order to face the Kaaba before this verse in revelation, although this verse comes first in the recitation; Ibn Abbas and others state this, and the Barāʾ report supports it.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أنها متقدمة في التلاوة، متأخرة في النزول، وأنه نزل قوله: قد نرى تقلب وجهك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Barāʾ report supports the later-revelation chronology; on it, the future means they persist in an objection already made, while reading سيقول as قال is too strained because of the future marker سـ.
rows.anchor: ويدل على هذا ويصححه حديث البراء المتقدم، الذي خرجه البخاري

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب، مجاهد، ابن جبير
rows.claim: They identify the foolish objectors as the Jews.
rows.anchor: والسفهاء: اليهود، قاله البراء بن عازب، ومجاهد، وابن جبير

rows.speaker: أبو صالح، عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies the objectors as Meccans, who claimed Muhammad missed his birthplace and would soon return to their religion; al-Zajjāj preferred this view.
rows.anchor: وأهل مكة قالوا: اشتاق محمد إلى مولده، وعن قريب يرجع إلى دينكم، رواه أبو صالح، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي، عن ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He identifies the objectors as hypocrites mocking the Muslims; the verse's wording also recalls the description of hypocrites in 2:13, or may cover the three groups mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: أو المنافقون قالوا: ذلك استهزاء بالمسلمين، ذكره السدي، عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: The qualifier من الناس specifies humans because سفه can describe lightly woven cloth, a light fast spear, and animals; without it, attributing speech to nonhumans could be metaphorical.
rows.anchor: وخص بقوله من الناس، لأن السفه أصله الخفة، يوصف به الجماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ما ولاهم refers to the Prophet and believers turned from their qibla; it is attributed to them because they had faced it for a long time.
rows.anchor: والضمير عائد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، والمؤمنين عن قبلتهم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Most exegetes say the change criticized was from Jerusalem to the Kaaba, but the author denies that this is unanimous.
rows.anchor: وأجمع المفسرون على أن هذه التولية كانت من بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some hold that the earlier qibla was the Kaaba, faced when prayer was first prescribed because it was Abraham's qibla; after the Prophet turned toward Jerusalem, Meccans reproached him for leaving it.
rows.anchor: بل قد ذهب قوم إلى أن هذه القبلة، التي عيب التحول منها إلى غيرها هي الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase التي كانوا عليها implies sustained commitment to facing the qibla; على is figurative, as though the qibla were something continuously borne or maintained.
rows.anchor: والاستعلاء هنا مجاز، وحكمته الهم لمواظبتهم على امتثال أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns may instead refer to the foolish objectors: Jews faced west, Christians east, and Arabs had no prayer direction, so they objected when Muhammad faced the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يحتمل أن يكون الضمير عائدا على السفهاء، فإنهم كانوا لا يعرفون إلا قبلة اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view, attributed to Ibn Abbas, says the Jerusalem qibla was established by recited revelation; the author also lists an unrecited divine command and divine permission to choose, with al-Rabīʿ saying the Prophet chose Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: الأول: عن ابن عباس، روي عنه أنه قال: أول ما نسخ من القرآن القبلة

rows.speaker: الحسن، عكرمة، أبو العالية
rows.claim: They hold that the Prophet chose Jerusalem by personal reasoning without revelation.
rows.anchor: أو باجتهاده بغير وحي، قاله الحسن وعكرمة وأبو العالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports give the Jerusalem-facing period as sixteen or seventeen months, nine or ten months, or thirteen months; another reckoning begins with the prescribed daily prayers after the Night Journey and ends in Rajab, Jumada, or mid-Shaʿban of year two.
rows.anchor: وكذلك اختلفوا في المدة التي صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها إلى بيت المقدس، فقيل: ستة عشر شهرا، أو سبعة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed two noon rakʿas, then turned toward the Kaaba for the last two.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى ركعتي الظهر، فانصرف بالآخرتين إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is evidence that the Qurʾan can abrogate Sunnah, since the Jerusalem-facing prayer was not prescribed in Qurʾanic text, and that abrogation is not a change of mind in God.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بهذه الآية على جواز نسخ السنة بالقرآن، إذ صلاته إلى بيت المقدس ليس فيها قرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command teaches the Prophet how to refute the objection: all directions belong to God, who may require worshippers to face whichever one He chooses as a qibla.
rows.anchor: أن الجهات كلها لله تعالى، يكلف عباده بما شاء أن يستقبل منها، وأن تجعل قبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: East refers to Jerusalem and west to the Kaaba, since the Kaaba lies west of Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: والمغرب بالكعبة، لأن الكعبة غربي بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يهدي من يشاء means those whom God wills to guide; هدى can take لام, إلى, or no preposition, and here it takes إلى.
rows.anchor: يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم: أي من يشاء هدايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes disagree whether the qibla was changed during the dawn, noon, or afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وقد اختلفوا في الصلاة التي حولت القبلة فيها، فقيل: الصبح، وقيل: الظهر، وقيل: العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He declines speculative explanations of the qibla change's wisdom when neither revelation nor sound reasoning supports them, warning that seeking causes for divine acts invites error.
rows.anchor: بأشياء لا يقوم على صحتها دليل، وعللوا ذلك بعلل لم يشر إليها الشرع، ولا قاد نحوها العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only wisdoms stated or indicated by revelation, or reached by sound reasoning, should be accepted.
rows.anchor: وأما ما نص الشرع على حكمته، أو أشار، أو قاد إليه النظر الصحيح

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some interpret the straight path here as the Kaaba qibla; the author says the apparent meaning is Islam and its laws, of which the Kaaba is one.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر قوله: صراط مستقيم بأنه القبلة التي هي الكعبة. والظاهر أنه ملة الإسلام وشرائعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وكذلك, the ك is comparative and ذلك is a demonstrative in the accusative, either modifying an omitted verbal noun or functioning circumstantially.
rows.anchor: الكاف: للتشبيه، وذلك: اسم إشارة، والكاف في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative ذلك points to the implied verbal noun of يهدي, namely الهداية, not to an earlier explicit noun; guidance means that God places a person on the straight path.
rows.anchor: لكن تقدم لفظ يهدي، وهو دال على المصدر، وهو الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison can mean that making the community just and excellent is a favor like guiding it through Muhammad and the truth he brought.
rows.anchor: وتبين أيضا من قوله: قل لله المشرق والمغرب إلى آخره، أن الله جعل قبلتهم خيرا من قبلة اليهود والنصارى، أو وسطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation compares making the community a middle community to God's special act of placing it on the straight path, a guidance granted only to whom He wills.
rows.anchor: شبه جعلهم أمة وسطا بجعلهم على الصراط المستقيم، أي جعلناكم أمة وسطا مثل ذلك الجعل الغريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations compare the community's excellence to its qibla being the best, or its geographic middle position between east and west, or the Kaaba's centrality on earth; the community is below prophets and above other nations.
rows.anchor: كما جعلنا قبلتكم خير القبل، جعلناكم خير الأمم. وقيل: المعنى كما جعلنا قبلتكم متوسطة بين المشرق والمغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls it far-fetched to make ذلك point to God's choosing Abraham in the world and compare that choosing to making this community middle.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أن ذلك إشارة إلى قوله تعالى: ولقد اصطفيناه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وسط means just, ascribed to the Prophet and widely repeated by exegetes; if the Prophetic report is sound, this meaning must govern the interpretation.
rows.anchor: ومعنى وسطا: عدولا، روي ذلك عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Other explanations take وسط as the best, or as religiously balanced between excess and neglect: unlike Christians the community does not deify a prophet, and unlike Jews it does not kill one.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خيار، أو قيل: متوسطين في الدين بين المفرط والمقصر

rows.speaker: جمهور المعتزلة
rows.claim: The majority of Muʿtazilites argue that communal consensus is authoritative because God describes this community as just and excellent, so its collective judgment must be binding.
rows.anchor: واحتج جمهور المعتزلة بهذه الآية على أن إجماع الأمة حجة

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most interpreters understand the community's witnessing as occurring in the afterlife, testifying for the prophets against the nations that denied them; this is stated in reports in al-Bukhari and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أحدها: ما عليه الأكثر من أنها في الآخرة، وهي شهادة هذه الأمة للأنبياء على أممهم الذين كذبوهم

rows.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
rows.claim: Al-Muntakhab says the Qadi criticized the hadith supporting afterlife testimony; the author identifies him as likely the Muʿtazilite ʿAbd al-Jabbār and says attacking an authentic hadith does not fit Sunni doctrine.
rows.anchor: وقد طعن القاضي في الحديث من وجوه، وذكروا وجوها ضعيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He regards the Qadi's criticism of the sound, authentic hadith as incompatible with Sunni doctrine.
rows.anchor: لأن الطعن في الحديث الثابت الصحيح لا يناسب مذاهب أهل السنة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some interpret the community's witnessing as taking place in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الشهادة تكون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say believers testify for one another at death; a Prophetic report describes people praising or condemning two deceased persons, the Prophet saying their fate was established and calling the community God's witnesses on earth; Muslim records it.
rows.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث من أنه مر بجنازة فأثني عليها خيرا، وبأخرى فأثني عليها شرا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains witnessing as presenting an argument against people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الشهادة الاحتجاج، أي لتكونوا محتجين على الناس، حكاه الزجاج

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that believers convey the revelation and religion they learned, as the Messenger conveyed them; على then means لام, as in 5:3.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لتنقلوا إليهم ما علمتموه من الوحي والدين كما نقله رسول الله

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A further interpretation makes the community's consensus a proof and the Messenger's witness a proof through his delivery of the message.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ليكون إجماعكم حجة، ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا، أي محتجا بالتبليغ

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the community bears witness for Muhammad against the nations, including Jews, Christians, and Magians.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لتكونوا شهداء لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم على الأمم، اليهود والنصارى والمجوس، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take it as worldly testimony in matters requiring upright witnesses; its grounds include direct observation, a truthful report, widespread knowledge, and inference, with examples including adultery, lineage, property, and evaluating witnesses.
rows.anchor: وأسباب هذه الشهادة، أي شهادة هذه العدول أربعة: بمعاينة، كالشهادة على الزنا

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd lists four groups who testify: angels recording deeds, prophets, Muhammad's community, and bodily limbs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن دريد: الإشهاد أربعة: الملائكة بإثبات أعمال العباد، والأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because physical sight and inward understanding are closely related, intellectual perception is called witnessing, the knower a witness, and evidence testimony because it makes the witness a witness; legally, testimony refers to a formal report about human rights.
rows.anchor: ولما كان بين الرؤية بالبصر والإدراك بالبصيرة مناسبة شديدة، سمي إدراك البصيرة: مشاهدة وشهودا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa takes the verse as evidence that Muslims are presumptively upright, understanding وسط as just and excellent.
rows.anchor: قالوا: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن الأصل في المسلمين العدالة، وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: بقية العلماء
rows.claim: Other scholars say uprightness is an acquired status established only by evidence; later Hanafi authorities adopted the majority position because people's conditions changed, except in hudud and retaliation cases.
rows.anchor: وقال بقية العلماء: العدالة وصف عارض لا يثبت إلا ببينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All agree that the Messenger here is Muhammad; interpretations of his witnessing include attesting that he delivered the message, their faith, being proof against them, or validating and purifying them.
rows.anchor: لا خلاف أن الرسول هنا هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وفي شهادته أقوال

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the community witnesses against all who abandon truth, while the Messenger serves as their validating and purifying witness; a report is also transmitted on this point.
rows.anchor: الرابع: تزكيته لهم وتعديله إياهم، قاله عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The لام in لتكونوا is either purposive or, for those who take it so, consequential: the community's excellence or justice follows from this testimony; the Messenger's testimony also confers great honor because the noblest creature witnesses for them.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله: لتكونوا هي، لام كي، أو لام الصيرورة عن من يرى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على suits a witness who oversees the person witnessed for; placing it after الناس follows ordinary word order, while moving it before شهيدا in عليكم شهيدا gives rhetorical latitude and lets شهيدا close the clause.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الشهيد كالرقيب على المشهود له، جيء بكلمة على

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the first على is fronted to emphasize the community's testimony over nations, while عليكم is delayed to mark the Messenger's exclusive testimony over them.
rows.anchor: وما ذهب إليه الزمخشري من أن تقديم على أولا، لأن الغرض فيه إثبات شهادتهم على الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects al-Zamakhsharī's exclusivity reading: moving an object or prepositional phrase forward does not itself prove restriction, and the claim lacks proof.
rows.anchor: وأن ذلك دعوى لا يقوم عليها برهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence reflects the event: the community testifies against the nations, then the Messenger is asked about his community and validates their testimony that the messengers delivered the message; if the readings permit an earlier Messenger testimony, its later mention is rhetorical gradation because it is more honorable.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أنهم يشهدون على الأمم، ثم يشهد الرسول عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Muhammad الرسول highlights his divine mission, and شهيد is an intensive form expressing more force than شاهد, شاهدين, or إشهادا.
rows.anchor: وأتى بلفظ الرسول، لما في الدلالة بلفظ الرسول على اتصافه بالرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes who understand شهيدا as one who validates the community and عليكم as لكم infer that a ruler's validation entails acceptance of testimony.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بقوله: ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا على أن التزكية تقتضي قبول الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here جعل means to convert, taking two objects: the original state is the first object and the resulting qibla the second; the Kaaba was first the qibla, then Jerusalem, then the Kaaba again.
rows.anchor: جعل هنا: بمعنى صير، فيتعدى لمفعولين: أحدهما القبلة، والآخر التي كنت عليها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead parses التي كنت عليها as the second object, says it is not an adjective of القبلة, and explains the verse as the return to the Meccan Kaaba to test people after the Prophet had faced Jerusalem to accommodate the Jews.
rows.anchor: ووهم الزمخشري في ذلك، فزعم أن التي كنت عليها: هو المفعول الثاني لجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He corrects al-Zamakhsharī's parsing: التي كنت عليها is the first object, not the second.
rows.anchor: وقد أوضحنا أن التي كنت عليها: هو المفعول الأول

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view makes the verse explain why Jerusalem was made the qibla: facing it was temporary, distinguishing the steadfast from the apostate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا بيان لحكمة جعل بيت المقدس قبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either the Kaaba or Jerusalem can be meant by التي كنت عليها, since the Prophet faced both at different times.
rows.anchor: وكل واحد من الكعبة وبيت المقدس صالح بأن يوصف بقوله: التي كنت عليها

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: If التي كنت عليها modifies القبلة, proposed omitted second objects are قبلة or منسوخة; another analysis supplies the omitted noun صرف and treats لنعلم as the second object, as in saying a person was struck for instruction.
rows.anchor: فقيل: تقديره: وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها قبلة إلا لنعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the relative clause as an adjective, القبلة can denote either the Kaaba or Jerusalem because the Prophet had faced each of them.
rows.anchor: وعلى كون التي صفة، يحتمل أن يراد بالقبلة: الكعبة، ويحتمل أن يراد بيت المقدس
